reasoning.text: The render reads cleanly as an FPGA NTT accelerator — open butterfly frame with all 8 copper multipliers and add/sub pairs exposed, glass BRAM banks down the left edge, exploded radix-4 BU and 10-fin heatsink lifted on posts well clear of the die, nothing floating off the ground line. The defects are not geometric but in fidelity: the scene literally cites the buggy additive bank map b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8 in bram_0/bram_1/addr_gen while the crossbar notes prove it collides at stride-512 and commits an XOR-fold instead; the exploded radix-4 BU showed THREE twiddle multipliers (the naive datapath) although the authoritative spec commits the optimized 2-mult count; the twiddle-ROM gave two contradictory address functions (block<<stage overflows a 1024-deep ROM); and the FSM listed three overlapping, contradictory state sets. These contradictions are exactly the reproducibility gaps — an engineer could not rebuild from the scene as-was.
gaps: The committed XOR-fold bank/offset and cyclic sigma_s are reproduction reconstructions that satisfy the named conflict-free property but are NOT the paper's actual (untranscribed Sec. III) functions — re-pin if the source mapping is recovered

The 2-multiplier radix-4 datapath (W3=W1*W2 chaining) reproduces the source's 33% claim by a plausible construction, not the paper's exact scheduled butterfly — verify against the source's datapath figure
Twiddle-ROM f(stage,block) and the rearranged twiddle-reuse loop are the committed CT-DIT convention, not the paper's specific rearranged-loop addressing

The central butterfly array is dense in the TOP view; a future pass could fan the 8 lanes apart or thin the add/sub boxes so each lane's mult->add/sub->reg chain is individually traceable from plan view

fields.before: Permutation crossbar (8x8) implementing the conflict-free mapping: each cycle it gathers up to 16 operands from the eight dual-port BRAM banks and routes them to the eight butterfly lanes, then accepts the 8 reduced results back over the return bus and writes them home — the read and write halves of the conflict-free read-modify-write loop.
fields.after: Permutation crossbar (8x8) implementing the conflict-free mapping: each cycle it gathers up to 16 operands from the eight dual-port BRAM banks and routes them to the eight butterfly lanes, then accepts the 8 reduced results back over the return bus and writes them home - the read and write halves of the conflict-free read-modify-write loop.

params.ports: 16 operand reads + 8 result writes per cycle: eight radix-2 butterflies x 2 operand reads = 16 reads, served by 8 dual-port BRAM banks (2 read ports each); 8 reduced results write back. Radix-4 mode gathers 4 operands per fused BU from 4 distinct banks (still 16 reads across the 4 active fused units).
params.per_stage_permutation: at radix-2 stage s (s=0..9) a butterfly pairs operands at indices (i, i+2^s); the crossbar applies read permutation sigma_s where operand-a of lane L is fetched from bank (L - s) mod 8 and operand-b from bank (L - s + R_s) mod 8 with R_s = ((2^s)>>3)+1; the write-back applies the inverse sigma_s^{-1} so reduced results return to their home banks
params.radix4_routing: a radix-4 BU gathers 4 operands (i, i+2^s, i+2^{s+1}, i+3*2^s) which b(i) guarantees fall in 4 distinct banks; the crossbar routes them to the 4 input ports of one fused lane-pair in a single cycle
params.sigma_s: crossbar lane l <- bank( base_s + l*stride_s ); per-stage permutation induced by bank_fn over the 8 lane indices

before.notes:
Reproduction conflict-free mapping: for B=8 banks the up-to-4 operands of any radix-2/4 butterfly at every stage land in distinct banks, so reads/writes never collide and no bit-reversal stage is needed. Port accounting: eight radix-2 butterflies require 16 simultaneous operand reads, so the banks MUST be dual-ported (2 read ports each) — a rebuilder provisioning single-port BRAM would halve throughput. The paper's exact bank-index/offset functions (its headline Sec. III result) are not transcribed in the source; this XOR/rotate-style map plus the rotation permutation sigma_s satisfy the asserted no-conflict property and are rebuildable by a CS student.
[conv] COMMITTED conflict-free map: bank(i)=XOR-fold of the four 3-bit groups of i, offset(i)=floor(i/8). This is a GF(2)-linear bank function, so for any power-of-two stride 2^k the two operands differ in exactly one address bit and bank(i) XOR bank(i+2^k) = fold(2^k) != 0 -> operands always in distinct banks. [calc] FIXES the verifier counterexample of the prior map b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8: there b(i+512)=b(i) (576 mod 8 = 0) so stride-512 operands collided; with XOR-fold fold(bit9)->bank bit0 = 1 != 0. (bank,offset) is a bijection on [0,1024) (offset fixes bits 9..3, low 3 bits XOR-map to all 8 banks). [source-missing] the paper's exact sigma_s crossbar permutation table per stage is not transcribed; the XOR-fold realizes the named property (per-stage 8-way distinctness) but may differ in routing from the paper's specific construction.

In radix-4 mode the config selector merges this lane pair so their two DSP multipliers and shared symmetric add/sub trees act as a single 4-operand BU computing y0..y3 with the 3 twiddles W1,W2,W3 and the constant j-rotator; four such yokes turn the eight radix-2 lanes into four radix-4 BUs.
fields.after: Radix-4 fusion yoke binding butterfly lanes 0 and 1 into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit - the architecture's headline contribution made physical. Four such yokes turn the eight radix-2 lanes into four radix-4 BUs.

params.primitive_root_psi: psi = g^6 = 11^6 mod 12289 = 1945 (order 2048; psi^1024 ≡ -1 mod 12289, i.e. negacyclic)

params.psi_inv: psi^{-1} mod q via Fermat (psi^{q-2}); INTT uses psi^{-i}/omega^{-k} twiddles together with N^-1 = 12277
params.psi_power_table_sample: entry[k] = psi^k mod 12289 with psi=1945: psi^0=1, psi^1=1945, psi^2=10302(=omega), psi^3=6320, psi^4=3400, ...; structural anchors psi^512=j (j^2≡12288≡-1), psi^1024≡12288≡-1 (negacyclic sign flip), psi^2048≡1; the omega table is the even subsequence omega^k = psi^(2k). The full 0..2047 table is generated by iterated multiply-by-1945-mod-12289 from this seed (bit-exact, no bit-reversal indexing).

params.psi_power_table_sample: entry[k] = psi^k mod 12289 with psi=1945: psi^0=1, psi^1=1945, psi^2=10302(=omega), psi^3=6320, psi^4=3400, ...; structural anchors psi^512=j (j^2≡12288≡-1), psi^1024≡12288≡-1 (negacyclic sign flip), psi^2048≡1; the omega table is the even subsequence omega^k = psi^(2k). The full 0..2047 table is generated by iterated multiply-by-1945-mod-12289 from this seed (bit-exact, no bit-reversal indexing).
params.stored: omega^k stage twiddles for k=0..N-1; psi^i pre-twist and psi^{-i} post-twist factors for the negacyclic case stored in the low/high halves
params.addressing: address = f(stage s, butterfly-block index) = (1<<s) + block, block in [0, 2^s); one fetch reused across all 8 lanes per block
params.table_contents: entry[s][block] = omega raised to the block's stage exponent (no bit-reversal indexing); negacyclic twist factors keyed by coefficient index i
params.addr_fn: f(stage,block) = (1<<stage) + block, block in [0, 2^stage), stage 0..9 -> address in [1,1024)

after.notes:
Depth N=1024 covers every stage twiddle without bit-reversal. Reproduction pins the concrete generator g=11 -> psi=1945 and the seed power table above so the ROM contents are bit-exact reproducible; the source states reuse via the rearranged loop but gives neither the table contents nor the primitive root, so these are reproduction-chosen values consistent with the negacyclic constraints psi^1024≡-1, psi^2048≡1.
[conv] CT/DIT merged-negacyclic layout (Longa-Naehrig style): single ROM of N=1024 entries holding psi^(brv(k)); at stage s the 2^s block twiddles occupy the contiguous range [2^s, 2^(s+1)) so f(stage,block)=(1<<stage)+block reads them in sequence and stays within the 1024-deep ROM. The earlier 'block<<stage' variant is RANGE-INVALID for a 1024-deep ROM (overflows for large s) and is purged. [src] psi=1945. [calc] entries are powers of 1945 mod 12289. [source-missing] the paper's exact f(stage,block) addressing under its rearranged loop may index differently; the (1<<stage)+block CT addressing above is the committed reproducible choice (only a seed table was implied).
[source-missing] exact rearranged twiddle-reuse loop address function f(stage,block). [conv] committed CT-DIT convention f(stage,block)=(1<<stage)+block so the address is concrete and range-valid; [src] single shared ROM (twiddle reuse) reduces footprint.

transitions: IDLE -> LOAD  [host start pulse]
LOAD -> STAGE_LOOP  [coefficient vector resident in banks]
STAGE_LOOP -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [enter next twiddle-sharing block]
TWIDDLE_FETCH -> BUTTERFLY  [w latched onto broadcast rail]
BUTTERFLY -> REDUCE  [lane products valid]
REDUCE -> WRITEBACK  [r in [0,q) from Barrett stage]
WRITEBACK -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [blocks remain in stage s]
WRITEBACK -> STAGE_LOOP  [stage done, s++ while s<S]
STAGE_LOOP -> INTT_STAGE_LOOP  [forward stages done AND INTT requested]
STAGE_LOOP -> DRAIN  [forward-only transform done]
INTT_STAGE_LOOP -> SCALE_N_INV  [inverse stages done]
SCALE_N_INV -> DRAIN  [coefficients scaled by N^-1]
DRAIN -> IDLE  [output FIFO emptied to host]

before.notes:
The factor-constant inner block is what lets one twiddle fetch be reused across all 8 lanes. The transition table and loop bounds here are reconstructed; the source asserts the 33%/20% savings only as a property and does not publish its state machine.

[src] read-modify-write interleaved-BRAM loop with 9-cycle pipeline fill per lane. SCALE state runs only for INTT (multiply by Ninv=12277). [conv] state names; rearranged-loop ordering delegated to addr_gen_unit + crossbar_network.

fields.before: EXPLODED ABOVE: aluminum heatsink baseplate that clamps onto the FPGA package lid covering the whole die, lifted high (y=3.6) on a long riser stub so it floats clearly above the datapath and the Barrett reduction spine — keeping the die floorplan and the +X pipeline-register column visible in the ISO X-ray rather than swallowing them; carries ten fins at 0.3 pitch.
fields.after: EXPLODED ABOVE: aluminum heatsink baseplate that clamps onto the FPGA package lid covering the whole die, lifted high (y=3.6) on a long riser stub so it floats clearly above the datapath and the Barrett reduction spine - keeping the die floorplan and the +X pipeline-register column visible in the ISO X-ray rather than swallowing them; carries ten fins at 0.3 pitch.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel radix-2 butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register; finally seat the four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes in the open gap between the multiplier and add/sub columns, each binding a lane-pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit so the eight radix-2 lanes reconfigure into four radix-4 BUs. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member abutting it, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame), keeping the read, return and twiddle channels on three separate heights; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the elevated rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one fused radix-4 butterfly unit onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the ten-fin exploded aluminum heatsink high onto its riser stub well above the die so the datapath below stays visible.
